/-!
# Resolution of singularities in characteristic $p$

A *resolution of singularities* of an algebraic variety $V$ is a non-singular variety $W$
together with a proper birational morphism $W \to V$. Hironaka (1964) proved that every variety
over a field of characteristic $0$ has a resolution of singularities. Over a field of
characteristic $p > 0$ the existence of a resolution is known in dimension at most $3$
(Abhyankar for curves and surfaces, Cossart–Piltant for threefolds) and is open in general.

Over a non-perfect field "non-singular" is taken to mean *regular*, i.e. all local rings are
regular local rings; this is the notion used in the positive-characteristic results cited below.
Properness of the resolution morphism excludes trivial solutions such as the inclusion of the
regular locus of $V$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Resolution of singularities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resolution_of_singularities)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Hir64] H. Hironaka, *Resolution of singularities of an algebraic variety over a field of
  characteristic zero. I, II*, Ann. of Math. 79 (1964).
- [CP08] V. Cossart, O. Piltant, *Resolution of singularities of threefolds in positive
  characteristic. I*, J. Algebra 320 (2008).
- [CP09] V. Cossart, O. Piltant, *Resolution of singularities of threefolds in positive
  characteristic. II*, J. Algebra 321 (2009).
- [Hau10] H. Hauser, *On the problem of resolution of singularities in positive characteristic
  (Or: a proof we are still waiting for)*, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 47 (2010).
-/

def IsBirational {W V : Scheme.{u}} (f : W ⟶ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ U : V.Opens, Dense (X := V) U ∧ Dense (X := W) (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) ∧ IsIso (f ∣_ U)
blocks.docstring:
A morphism of schemes `f : W ⟶ V` is *birational* if it restricts to an isomorphism
`f ⁻¹ᵁ U ≅ U` for some dense open `U ⊆ V` whose preimage `f ⁻¹ᵁ U` is dense in `W`.
For integral schemes this says that `f` induces an isomorphism of function fields.

justification.closest_existing_considered: AlgebraicGeometry.IsDominant, Scheme.RationalMap / PartialMap (no notion of invertible rational map), Scheme.functionField and Hom.stalkMap at genericPoint (alternative 'dominant + iso of function fields' definition, equivalent for integral schemes).
justification.name: ResolutionOfSingularities.IsBirational
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no birational-morphism predicate. Defined as existence of a dense open U of the target with dense preimage such that the restriction f ∣_ U is an isomorphism.

claims.decomposer_note: Made precise by the article's lead: for every field k of characteristic p > 0 and every algebraic variety V over k (integral separated scheme of finite type over k), there exists a non-singular variety W over k with a proper birational morphism W → V; 'non-singular' should be formalized as regular (not smooth over k, since k need not be perfect), the Prop quantifies over all positive characteristics and all dimensions (dimensions ≤ 3 are known by Abhyankar/Cossart–Piltant, and only dim ≥ 4 is open, but the assertion as a whole is open), and 'proper' is essential to exclude the trivial open-immersion of the regular locus.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the slot faithfully and compile (verified); they differ only in packaging. c06 was chosen because it is the most literal and idiomatic: it uses Mathlib's `Scheme.Over`/`Hom.IsOver` machinery so V and W are explicitly k-schemes and f is explicitly a k-morphism; it bundles 'algebraic variety over k' (integral + separated + locally of finite type + quasi-compact structure map) into a documented `IsVariety` structure and requires it of both V and W (matching 'non-singular variety W'); non-singular is regular (Noetherian stalks with Krull dimension = dim_κ m/m², not smooth over k); properness is Mathlib's `IsProper`; birational is 'isomorphism over a dense open of V with dense preimage', which for integral schemes is equivalent to the function-field definition used by c01/c03/c07 and the two-dense-opens formulation of c05/c08; char p > 0 is `[Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]`, with no dimension bound so the whole Prop is open. It also carries API lemmas for the bespoke definitions. `#print` confirmed the elaborated statement is ∀ k field, ∀ p prime with CharP k p, ∀ k-variety V, ∃ regular k-variety W and proper birational k-morphism f : W ⟶ V. No edits were needed.

context: In algebraic geometry, the problem of resolution of singularities asks whether every algebraic variety V has a resolution, which is a non-singular variety W with a proper birational map W→V. For varieties over fields of characteristic 0, this was proved by Heisuke Hironaka in 1964; while for varieties of dimension at least 4 over fields of characteristic p, it is an open problem.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The table's single slot and its notes (regular rather than smooth, all positive characteristics and all dimensions, properness essential) were followed exactly.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Resolution of singularities in characteristic $p$

A *resolution of singularities* of an algebraic variety $V$ is a non-singular variety $W$
together with a proper birational morphism $W \to V$. Hironaka (1964) proved that every variety
over a field of characteristic $0$ has a resolution of singularities. Over a field of
characteristic $p > 0$ the existence of a resolution is known in dimension at most $3$
(Abhyankar for curves and surfaces, Cossart–Piltant for threefolds) and is open in general.

Over a non-perfect field "non-singular" is taken to mean *regular*, i.e. all local rings are
regular local rings; this is the notion used in the positive-characteristic results cited below.
Properness of the resolution morphism excludes trivial solutions such as the inclusion of the
regular locus of $V$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Resolution of singularities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resolution_of_singularities)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Hir64] H. Hironaka, *Resolution of singularities of an algebraic variety over a field of
  characteristic zero. I, II*, Ann. of Math. 79 (1964).
- [CP08] V. Cossart, O. Piltant, *Resolution of singularities of threefolds in positive
  characteristic. I*, J. Algebra 320 (2008).
- [CP09] V. Cossart, O. Piltant, *Resolution of singularities of threefolds in positive
  characteristic. II*, J. Algebra 321 (2009).
- [Hau10] H. Hauser, *On the problem of resolution of singularities in positive characteristic
  (Or: a proof we are still waiting for)*, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 47 (2010).
-/

open AlgebraicGeometry CategoryTheory IsLocalRing

namespace ResolutionOfSingularities

universe u

/-- A local ring `R` is a *regular local ring* if it is Noetherian and its Krull dimension equals
the dimension of its cotangent space $\mathfrak{m} / \mathfrak{m}^2$ over its residue field
$R / \mathfrak{m}$. -/
structure IsRegularLocalRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] : Prop where
  isNoetherianRing : IsNoetherianRing R
  ringKrullDim_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace :
    ringKrullDim R = Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R)

/-- A field is a regular local ring. -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem isRegularLocalRing_of_field (K : Type*) [Field K] : IsRegularLocalRing K where
  isNoetherianRing := inferInstance
  ringKrullDim_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace := by
    rw [ringKrullDim_eq_zero_of_field, finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_zero]
    rfl

/-- A scheme `X` is *regular* (or *non-singular*) if the local ring $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ at every
point `x` of `X` is a regular local ring. -/
def IsRegular (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : X, IsRegularLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)

/-- A morphism of schemes `f : W ⟶ V` is *birational* if it restricts to an isomorphism
`f ⁻¹ᵁ U ≅ U` for some dense open `U ⊆ V` whose preimage `f ⁻¹ᵁ U` is dense in `W`.
For integral schemes this says that `f` induces an isomorphism of function fields. -/
def IsBirational {W V : Scheme.{u}} (f : W ⟶ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ U : V.Opens, Dense (X := V) U ∧ Dense (X := W) (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) ∧ IsIso (f ∣_ U)

/-- An isomorphism of schemes is birational. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem IsBirational.of_isIso {W V : Scheme.{u}} (f : W ⟶ V) [IsIso f] : IsBirational f :=
  ⟨⊤, by simp [dense_univ], by simp [dense_univ], inferInstance⟩

/-- A scheme `V` over a field `k` is an *(algebraic) variety over `k`* if it is integral,
separated over `k` and of finite type (locally of finite type and quasi-compact) over `k`. -/
structure IsVariety (k : Type u) [Field k] (V : Scheme.{u}) [V.Over (Spec (.of k))] : Prop where
  isIntegral : IsIntegral V
  isSeparated : IsSeparated (V ↘ Spec (.of k))
  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType (V ↘ Spec (.of k))
  quasiCompact : QuasiCompact (V ↘ Spec (.of k))

/-- **Resolution of singularities in characteristic $p$.**
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$ and let $V$ be an algebraic variety over $k$
(an integral separated scheme of finite type over $k$). Then there is a regular variety $W$
over $k$ and a proper birational $k$-morphism $W \to V$.

This is known when $\dim V \le 3$ (Abhyankar, Cossart–Piltant) and open when $\dim V \ge 4$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 14]
theorem resolution_of_singularities (k : Type u) [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    (V : Scheme.{u}) [V.Over (Spec (.of k))] (hV : IsVariety k V) :
    ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (_ : W.Over (Spec (.of k))) (f : W ⟶ V),
      IsVariety k W ∧ IsRegular W ∧ f.IsOver (Spec (.of k)) ∧ IsProper f ∧
        IsBirational f := by
  sorry

end ResolutionOfSingularities

items: 'Non-singular' is formalized as REGULAR (every stalk O_{W,x} is a regular local ring), not 'smooth over k', following the decomposition notes; over a perfect field the two agree, over a non-perfect field regular is the notion used by Abhyankar/Cossart–Piltant.

Regular local ring is defined as: Noetherian local ring with ringKrullDim R = Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R) (Krull dimension equals dim_κ 𝔪/𝔪²). This is the textbook definition; Noetherianity is included so finrank's junk value on infinite-dimensional spaces is unreachable.

'Algebraic variety over k' = integral scheme whose structure morphism to Spec k is separated, locally of finite type and quasi-compact (i.e. of finite type), bundled as the Prop-structure IsVariety k V. The article's lead does not fix the convention; this is the one given in the decomposition table (integral separated scheme of finite type over k).

'Birational morphism' is defined as: there is a dense open U ⊆ V whose preimage f⁻¹U is dense in W and such that the restriction f ∣_ U : f⁻¹U ⟶ U is an isomorphism. For integral schemes and proper (hence separated, finite type) f this is equivalent to the classical definition (dominant + isomorphism of function fields, Stacks 01RN/0BAB). The density of f⁻¹U is redundant for integral W but makes the general definition more robust.

Characteristic p > 0 is encoded as (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]. For a field, CharP k p with p ≠ 0 forces p prime, so this is equivalent to 'characteristic p ≠ 0'; characteristic 0 (Hironaka's theorem) is excluded, as in the list entry.
The statement quantifies over all positive characteristics and all dimensions (no dimension restriction), so the Prop as a whole is open even though dimension ≤ 3 is known.

W is required to carry a k-structure with f a k-morphism (f.IsOver (Spec (.of k))) and to be a k-variety itself; these follow automatically from W regular + f proper birational over a k-variety, but are stated explicitly to match 'non-singular variety W over k with a proper birational morphism W → V'.
k and all schemes live in the same universe u (k : Type u, Scheme.{u}), as required by Spec (.of k).

The bespoke definitions (IsRegularLocalRing, IsRegular, IsBirational, IsVariety) are placed in the problem file because only one file could be written; a maintainer may prefer to move IsRegularLocalRing and IsBirational to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Each has an API lemma (a field is a regular local ring; an isomorphism is birational).

reviewer_notes: The list entry is a bare phrase; every candidate (and the decomposition table) made it precise via the article lead: every variety over a field of char p > 0 admits a proper birational morphism from a non-singular variety. Ambiguities resolved the same way by all candidates: 'variety' = integral separated finite-type k-scheme (Stacks convention, as the table prescribes); 'non-singular' = regular (correct since k need not be perfect; Abhyankar/Cossart–Piltant produce regular models); 'birational' formalized bespoke since Mathlib has none — the dense-open-isomorphism and generic-stalk-isomorphism variants are equivalent for integral schemes. Mathlib in this checkout has no IsRegularLocalRing, regular scheme, birational, or single finite-type class (LocallyOfFiniteType + QuasiCompact used), so bespoke definitions were unavoidable; they are kept in the problem file since the deliverable is a single file — a maintainer may wish to move IsRegularLocalRing/IsBirational to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Checked: quantifier order, no vacuous hypotheses (Spec k itself is a k-variety), IsRegularLocalRing has no junk-value issue (Noetherianity makes finrank and Krull dimension finite), `≫` clash with the repo's asymptotic notation does not affect the chosen file (c06 uses `↘`/`IsOver`). Candidates c01/c04 leave W's variety-ness implicit (follows from properness) — also faithful but less literal; c04 puts @[category test] on an instance, which is unusual. No candidate omitted the slot; no objections to the decomposition were raised, and I have none.
